verdicts.trueWording: it marks the real beginning of my writing career

Section headed 'Wolfe's comments from the Introduction to Storeys from the Old Hotel'; the full sentence begins "'Trip, Trap' was the first story I ever sold Damon Knight for his Orbit series". Note the wiki is a secondary transcription of the 1988 introduction, not the book itself.

verdicts.trueWording: Wolfe, and Pei, and Emshwiller tell of lives lived on the edge
verdicts.note: Raw scan fetched (gwern, 200, 7.5MB) and text-extracted with pdftotext. Le Guin's Introduction, printed page 11; the sentence ends 'of hope, or a little over the edge.' Title page confirms Le Guin and Kidd as editors, Pocket Books 1980.

verdicts.trueWording: they are all outsiders, threshold people, artists of the liminal, edge-dwellers
verdicts.note: Same scan, Introduction, bottom of printed page 10 running to page 11 (the claim's citation says p. 11). Full clause: 'In fact, fame or no fame, I believe they are all...' — 'all' covers every contributor, Wolfe included, and the title page credits Le Guin and Kidd as the editors who selected them.

verdicts.trueWording: I have agreed to introduce the book entire
verdicts.note: Same scan, Introduction. The immediately preceding sentence assigns the per-story presentation to Virginia (Kidd) as the writers are gone round in turn, so both limbs of the division of labour are stated. One citation discrepancy: the passage sits on printed page 11, not the p. 12 the claim cites.

verdicts.trueWording: His short story hereunder is a den of iniquity
verdicts.note: Same scan, unsigned headnote facing 'Suzanne Delage' (printed page 94 of the scan sequence), ending 'no one else could have written it.' The headnote carries no byline, so the attribution to Kidd rests on Le Guin's own statement earlier in the same volume that Virginia presents each story while Le Guin introduces the book entire — an inference from the book's stated division of labour, not from a signature.

verdicts.trueWording: Introduction by Ursula K. Le Guin
verdicts.note: Le Guin Foundation page fetched live (200, 102KB) and tag-stripped. Table of Contents lists the introduction line verbatim and '“Suzanne Delage” by Gene Wolfe'; the blurb says the volume was edited by Le Guin and Virgina [sic] Kidd and is 'an original collection', and the page states it was originally published by Pocket Books in 1980 — supporting co-editor, 1980, first appearance and introduction.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that Interfaces was the SECOND anthology Le Guin hand-picked with Kidd — this page calls it her first
verdicts.trueWording: the first anthology ever edited by Ursula K. Le Guin
verdicts.note: Le Guin Foundation page fetched live (200, 105KB). The quoted phrase 'Hand picked by Ursula K. Le Guin' is verbatim, Virginia Kidd is named as co-selector in the same sentence, '“A Criminal Proceeding” by Gene Wolfe' is in the Table of Contents, and the page dates it to Ace Books 1980 — so the Wolfe-selection limb and the 1980 limb hold. But the same blurb calls Interfaces her first anthology, which the ordinal 'second' contradicts rather than merely omitting; the page gives no basis for ordering it after Edges.

verdicts.trueWording: Ursula K. Le Guin and Brian Attebery's Norton Book of Science Fiction
verdicts.note: Le Guin Foundation page fetched live (200, 110KB). The Table of Contents carries '“Feather Tigers” by Gene Wolfe' verbatim, the blurb credits the volume to Le Guin and Attebery, and the page states it was originally published in 1993 by W.W. Norton. All three limbs supported.
